bib.title: AI Engineering, Chapter 4. Evaluate AI Systems

question: How should a team define evaluation criteria for an AI application, choose a model among many candidates and public benchmarks, and build an evaluation pipeline it can trust?
contributions: Four buckets of evaluation criteria: domain-specific capability, generation capability, instruction-following, cost and latency
A four-step model-selection workflow and seven axes for the API versus self-host decision
A critique of public benchmarks and leaderboards (selection, correlation, aggregation, contamination)
A three-step recipe for an evaluation pipeline: evaluate all components, write a guideline, pick methods and data

limits: Benchmark and leaderboard facts are dated to 2023-2024: the author notes Hugging Face replaced its six benchmarks in June 2024 and that new benchmarks will soon saturate too.
Most numbers are reported from other work or hypothetical (the 80/90/98% automation mapping, the Table 4-3 criteria); the chapter runs no experiments of its own.
The author concedes no perfect evaluation method exists and that a high-dimensional system cannot be captured by one or few scores.
Anecdotes (20% to 70% accuracy after task decomposition, the VMO hallucination finding) carry no dataset or sample size.
The chapter says a statistical significance test could set sample size but 'it's hard to know the true score distribution', so Table 4-7 is a rough rule only.
Table 4-5 as printed is truncated at the GSM-8K column and is not symmetric (HellaSwag-TruthfulQA is 0.4809 in one row, 0.4228 in the other).
practices: Define evaluation criteria before building (evaluation-driven development) (Evaluation Criteria).
Group criteria into domain-specific capability, generation capability, instruction-following and cost/latency (Evaluation-driven development).
Use exact evaluation such as functional correctness for coding and close-ended tasks, and keep efficiency (runtime, memory) in the check (Domain-Specific Capability).
Freeze the prompt format when scoring MCQs, because small changes in spacing or phrasing change answers (Domain-Specific Capability).
Verify factual consistency against context (local) or open knowledge (global); use AI judges, SelfCheckGPT, SAFE or an NLI scorer (Factual consistency).
Analyse where the model hallucinates (niche knowledge, nonexistent things) and weight the benchmark toward those queries (Tip, Factual consistency).
Curate your own instruction-following benchmark with your own instructions, such as YAML output (Tip, Instruction-following criteria).
Check that a roleplaying model stays in character on both style and knowledge, including negative knowledge (Roleplaying).
For cost and latency, filter by non-negotiable requirements first, then pick the best of the rest; separate must-have from nice-to-have latency (Cost and Latency).
Follow four steps: filter hard attributes, narrow with public information, run your own evaluation pipeline, monitor in production (Model Selection Workflow).
Decide API versus self-hosting along seven axes: data privacy, data lineage, performance, functionality, cost, control, on-device (Open source models versus model APIs).
Check the license for commercial use, user-count restrictions and permission to train on outputs (Open source, open weight, and model licenses).
Treat public benchmarks as a filter for bad models, not a way to find the best one; check benchmark correlation and avoid plain averaging blindly (Benchmark selection and aggregation).
Assume public benchmarks are contaminated; detect with n-gram overlap or perplexity and disclose clean-sample performance (Handling data contamination).
Evaluate every component and the end-to-end output, per turn and per task (Step 1).
Write an evaluation guideline with scoring rubrics and examples per score, validated with humans, and tie metrics to business metrics and a usefulness threshold (Step 2).
Mix cheap classifiers on all data with expensive judges on a sample; use logprobs when available; keep human evaluation in production (Step 3, Select evaluation methods).
Slice evaluation data and keep multiple evaluation sets (production distribution, known-failure, user-error, out-of-scope) (Annotate evaluation data).
Bootstrap the evaluation set to test whether its size is enough (Annotate evaluation data).
Set the AI judge's temperature to 0 and log the evaluation data, rubric, prompt and sampling configuration (Evaluate your evaluation pipeline, Iterate).
